members.work: retired teacher, runs the parish newsletter
members.thread: A retired teacher who runs the parish newsletter, from the Study.

members.name: Hagop
members.thread: A retired developer with two consulting clients, working from the Family Room sofa.

members.name: Nare
members.thread: An eleven-year-old who reads, writes and looks things up.

character.lede: A raised periwinkle house of lap siding stands over a dark-brick garage storey, reached by a long brick stair with white balusters. Stepped board-and-batten gables, a dormer and a red-brick chimney crown the street front.

spots.line: A tuxedo sofa, a slipper chair and nesting tables make the study.
A media credenza, a wall screen and a loveseat fill the family room downstairs.
A workbench and a bicycle share the garage under the house.

facts.style: Raised periwinkle lap-siding house over a dark-brick garage storey: a front-gabled wing under a shingled pent skirt on white pilasters, the pale glazed front door in the recess up a long brick stair with white balusters, stepped board-and-batten cross gables, a dormer and a red-brick chimney, Italian cypress, arborvitae and birch

character.truths: The Core sits on a desk in the Study upstairs. The living room and the family room downstairs each have a television. The kitchen has an island. The front door is up a long brick stair.

joplin: [note] Joplin Server only; the Joplin apps are separate.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
marketplace: Joplin Server carries its own Personal Use License: not open source and limited for business use.
forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
paperless: [note] AI features are off by default. If you turn them on they can use a local model.
[note] Office document conversion is not wired up in this build; OCR and archiving of PDFs and scans works.
libreoffice: [note] The listing is generic. Name the suite, not specific features.
[note] ONLYOFFICE Desktop Editors does the same job: one suite per household.
kimai: Do not call it a billing or tax tool
mealie: [note] Pasting a recipe URL fetches that web page. Everything it saves stays on your Core.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
pasting a URL fetches that web page
booklore: [cloud-link] Fetches metadata and covers from outside.
jellyfin: [note] Plays your own files. Say that, not "Netflix".
[claims] Do not say it plays copyrighted material from anywhere.
Plays your own media only: never "streams any movie".
QA capture is the setup wizard with a container id as the server name; the gallery frame is a demo library with lurid exploitation film posters: neither usable.
project-nomad: [public-access] Ships without authentication. For trusted home networks only. Never describe it as exposed.
[note] amd64 only (fine on the Core). Internet is needed once for setup and downloads.
[claims] Educational content comes from third-party sources. Do not promise grades.
Ships without authentication: home network only, never described as exposed.

[cloud-link] It can also connect to cloud models with an API key. Leave that off.
[note] Wired to the Core's local model by the Hub (hub_integration inference). Say "a model on the Core"; never claim it matches a hosted model and never give a speed figure.

Hub wires it to the local model.

Watching away from home is remote access: not claimed.

docuseal: [claims] Do not call signatures legally binding.
[note] Signers outside your home network need access to your Core.
Do not call signatures legally binding
